chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from his brother al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a man is affected by janābah and wants to perform ghusl, then let him pour water over his two palms and wash them below the elbows, then put his hand into his vessel, then wash his private part, then let him pour over his head three times, each time a palmful, then strike with a palmful of water upon his chest and a palmful between his shoulders, then let him pour water over his entire body. So whatever splashes from his water into his vessel after he has done what I have described, there is no harm in it.

key_terms.إِنَائِهِ: his vessel or container holding the water
key_terms.الْغُسْلَ: the ritual bath performed for purification
key_terms.الْمِرْفَقِ: the elbow; here indicating washing the hands below it
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.فَرْجَهُ: his private part, to be washed before completing ghusl
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection in it
key_terms.كَفَّيْهِ: his two palms, used here for the initial washing and measuring water
key_terms.يُفِيضُ: he pours abundantly over, referring to washing the whole body

ai.seo_question: What is the proper method of performing ghusl for janābah, and does splashed water invalidate the vessel water?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the procedure of ghusl after janābah, beginning with washing the hands and private part, then pouring water over the head and body. It also clarifies that water splashing back into the vessel during this process does not make its use problematic.
